framework: Systems Thinking

# Shared-ride scheduling attempt

Three months ago the clinic tried grouping referral patients by pickup village and scheduling a shared ride rather than relying on the daily van's first-come seating. On paper it should have raised capacity without adding a vehicle, since a ride shared by four patients from the same village uses the same fuel and driver time as a ride for one. In practice the scheme lasted six weeks before it quietly stopped running, and it is worth being honest about why.

The scheduling depended on patients confirming a pickup time two days ahead, but the confirmation channel was the same unreliable phone coverage that undermines the appointment reminders elsewhere in this room's notes. When two of four expected riders failed to confirm, the driver, reasonably, treated the trip as uncertain and often skipped it rather than risk an empty run. The fix people keep proposing is a better confirmation channel, but nobody has asked the more basic systems question: what happens to the whole schedule when any single link in it depends on the one piece of infrastructure everyone already knows is unreliable.
